label: ercot185 shaped partial
definition: ercot-185 A/B ARM: the fault-3 day-shaped partial-outage plateau derate (ercot_partial_outage_shaped_derate=true) on the run181 keeper recipe. Pairs with ercot185_shapedcontrol_A. KEEPER (ercot-185): the fault-3 partial-layer construction repair — the CAMPD partial-outage plateau stops applying a multi-week median of daily maxima as an hourly ceiling and carries a day-resolved, median-preserving profile instead (zero new scalars). C3b-2024 0.205 -> 0.160 (PASS); 2023/2025 inert. Promoted under the owner's structural standard over a REJECTED-AS-ARMED gate verdict (G-SHED, G-C3c).
market_story: COAL and ST_GAS at partially-derated multi-unit plants: a plant with some units out does not sit at one flat capability for six weeks. Its usable ceiling tracks what the remaining units can actually deliver day by day — units return from and go back into work, ambient conditions move, and the plant's own CEMS record shows it reaching well above its multi-week average on individual afternoons (W A Parish ran 0.78 of its coal pmax on 2024-04-28 inside a window the model capped at 0.36). The market buys that real afternoon capability; the flat plateau forbade it, and the same flat plateau also LET the plant offer more than it could deliver on the window's deepest days. Arming the day-resolved profile puts both halves back: the plant is available when it demonstrably was, and unavailable when it demonstrably was not, with the window's measured average level unchanged. That is why the correction is two-sided (~50/50 up and down) and why it re-prices April-May 2024 — the maintenance season — without moving 2023 or 2025 annual energy by more than 0.5% in any class.
